EV-001.section: §3 Differential diagnosis & triage matrix for acute cough
EV-001.quote: Acute Cough: Present for less than 3 weeks.
EV-001.paraphrase: BTS duration categories: acute <3 weeks, subacute 3–8 weeks, chronic >8 weeks.

EV-002.quote: cough is typically self-limiting, resolving within 3 to 4 weeks
EV-002.paraphrase: Most cough is self-limiting and resolves in 3–4 weeks; basis for reassurance advice.

EV-003.quote: these presentations must be classified and managed as productive coughs
EV-003.paraphrase: A patient who brings up no sputum but "can feel it in the chest" is managed as a productive (chesty) cough.

EV-004.quote: Patients presenting with a non-acute cough (exceeding 3 weeks) who are not systemically unwell should be referred for further medical investigation.
EV-004.paraphrase: Non-acute cough (>3 weeks) needs referral for investigation.

EV-005.quote: Chest pain, haemoptysis, pain on inspiration, severe dyspnoea, or prominent wheezing
EV-005.paraphrase: Chest pain, haemoptysis, pain on inspiration, severe dyspnoea or prominent wheezing → urgent same-day referral (ED or GP by severity).

EV-006.quote: Cough duration > 3 weeks or recurring cough episodes
EV-006.paraphrase: Cough >3 weeks or recurring episodes → elective GP referral as soon as practicable.

EV-007.quote: Persistent nocturnal cough in pediatric patients
EV-007.paraphrase: Persistent night-time cough in a child (possible uncontrolled asthma) → refer as soon as practicable.

EV-008.quote: Unexplained anorexia or significant weight loss
EV-008.paraphrase: Unexplained anorexia or significant weight loss → refer as soon as practicable (TB, carcinoma, systemic disease).

EV-009.paraphrase: Debilitating symptoms in an older adult → urgent same-day referral.

EV-010.section: §3 Systematic decision logic for cough evaluation (flowchart)
EV-010.paraphrase: Source flowchart: >3 w → referral; productive with haemoptysis → immediate referral; mucoid/purulent → debilitating or older adult → urgent referral, mild → treat; dry sudden onset with fever/cold → viral URTI (treat); periodic → postnasal drip (treat) or allergy/asthma (refer if family history).

EV-011.quote: Generally indicates viral infection; does not routinely require antibiotic referral.
EV-011.paraphrase: Clear/white sputum is of little consequence; yellow/green/brown is generally viral; rust → pneumococcal pneumonia; pink → pulmonary oedema; dark red → suspicious of carcinoma; a single bright-red event is non-serious and needs no referral.

EV-012.quote: Indicative of bronchiectasis or a localized lung abscess.
EV-012.paraphrase: Thin frothy sputum suggests left ventricular failure; offensive/foul-smelling sputum suggests bronchiectasis or lung abscess.

EV-013.section: §3 Very unlikely causes – carcinoma of the lung
EV-013.quote: Any patient >40 years with two or more of these signs (or one sign in a smoker) requires urgent referral.
EV-013.paraphrase: Over 40: ≥2 of haemoptysis, dyspnoea, chest pain, anorexia, weight loss, fatigue — or ≥1 in a smoker — needs urgent referral.

EV-014.quote: Older adults may be afebrile and present solely with confusion.
EV-014.paraphrase: Pneumonia: rapid onset, rust sputum, high fever, pleuritic pain; older adults may present only with confusion. Assessed with CRB-65 (prescriber role).

EV-015.quote: Exacerbations involve acute drops in functional activity and severe dyspnoea, requiring GP referral for potential antibiotics and corticosteroids.
EV-015.paraphrase: COPD exacerbation (acute drop in activity, severe breathlessness) → GP referral.

EV-016.quote: Occurs in up to 16% of patients taking ACE inhibitors.
EV-016.paraphrase: ACE-inhibitor cough: up to 16%, onset hours to >1 year, resolves 3–4 weeks after withdrawal; NSAIDs, sitagliptin, CCBs and beta-blockers are rarer causes.

EV-017.quote: Sudden onset, minimal sputum, accompanied by fever and cold symptoms (duration 7–10 days)
EV-017.paraphrase: Viral URTI: sudden onset, little sputum, fever and cold symptoms, lasts 7–10 days, cough often worse in the evening.

EV-018.paraphrase: Upper airway cough syndrome: runny/blocked nose, throat clearing, itchy throat; allergic form is dry, worse at night, seasonal; treated with antihistamines and/or decongestants.

EV-019.quote: Symptoms are variable, intermittent, nocturnal, and provoked by triggers (allergens, exercise, cold air).
EV-019.paraphrase: Asthma / cough-variant asthma: variable, nocturnal cough provoked by triggers.

EV-020.quote: Violent, severe cough with a characteristic seal-like barking quality, accompanied by inter-episodic breathlessness and stridor.
EV-020.paraphrase: Croup: young children, night-time barking cough with stridor and breathlessness. (No explicit referral directive — GAP-12.)

EV-021.quote: concluding there is no high-quality evidence supporting their clinical effectiveness in acute cough
EV-021.paraphrase: Cochrane (Smith 2014): no high-quality evidence that OTC cough medicines work in acute cough; dextromethorphan is the only OTC centrally acting antitussive for dry cough (UK context).

EV-022.quote: Two trials demonstrated significant reductions in cough frequency and effort
EV-022.paraphrase: 2 of 3 adult RCTs showed fewer coughing bouts (8–10 per 30 min); third showed no benefit. Causes sedation; serotonin syndrome risk with serotonergic drugs.

EV-023.quote: its established safety profile and lack of drug interactions justify its supply for chesty coughs
EV-023.paraphrase: Trials conflict (n=239 positive; n=65 null; ER n=378 null at day 7) but safety and no interactions justify supply for chesty cough.

EV-024.quote: Non-sedating second-generation antihistamines show no benefit over placebo in acute cough
EV-024.paraphrase: Diphenhydramine efficacy in acute cough is not unequivocally substantiated; non-sedating antihistamines show no benefit.

EV-025.quote: honey administered for up to 3 days is superior to placebo or no treatment in reducing pediatric cough duration and severity
EV-025.paraphrase: Cochrane (Oduwole 2018; 6 trials, n=899 children): honey for up to 3 days reduces cough duration and severity; demulcents are inert and soothe the pharynx.

EV-026.quote: Thyme-containing remedies (e.g., Bronchostop) cannot be routinely recommended based on current clinical evidence.
EV-026.paraphrase: Herbal cough products have only very low-quality evidence; not routinely recommended.

EV-027.quote: Clinicians should avoid recommending multi-ingredient preparations, favoring targeted single-agent interventions instead.
EV-027.paraphrase: Avoid multi-ingredient cough products (illogical combinations, sub-therapeutic doses); use single agents.

EV-028.quote: Heated steam provides modest symptomatic comfort but carries a minor risk of nasal mucosal discomfort.
EV-028.paraphrase: Steam inhalation: conflicting evidence, modest comfort, minor nasal discomfort risk.

EV-029.quote: MODEST / MIXED EVIDENCE: Guaifenesin, Dextromethorphan, Benzydamine Spray.
EV-029.paraphrase: Source evidence tiers: strong — systemic analgesics, honey (paediatric cough); modest/mixed — guaifenesin, dextromethorphan; poor — oral phenylephrine etc.

EV-030.quote: None reported,None of clinical significance,None,Pregnancy: OK Breastfeeding: OK
EV-030.paraphrase: Guaifenesin: >6 y 100 mg four times daily; >12 y/adults 200 mg four times daily; no common side effects or significant interactions; OK in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

EV-031.quote: (Not for 12–18 yrs with breathing problems),"Drowsiness, sedation"
EV-031.paraphrase: Dextromethorphan: >12 y, 10 mL four times daily (strength not stated — GAP-01); not for 12–18 y with breathing problems; drowsiness; sedation potentiated by alcohol, opioids, anxiolytics, hypnotics, antidepressants; serotonin syndrome with MAOIs, SSRIs, tramadol; care in asthma; avoid 3rd trimester; breastfeeding OK short periods, monitor infant.

EV-032.quote: "Sedation, dry mouth, dizziness, headache, nausea, constipation"
EV-032.paraphrase: Diphenhydramine: >6 y (dose not stated — GAP-03); sedation, dry mouth, dizziness, headache, nausea, constipation; CNS depression with alcohol, opioids, sedatives, hypnotics, TCAs; care in glaucoma and prostate enlargement; pregnancy disputed; breastfeeding may reduce supply and sedate infant.

EV-033.quote: Simple Linctus (Demulcent),> 1 month ( 3–4 times daily),None,None,None,Pregnancy: OK Breastfeeding: OK
EV-033.paraphrase: Simple linctus: >1 month, 3–4 times daily (volume not stated — GAP-02); no side effects or interactions listed; OK in pregnancy and breastfeeding.

EV-034.quote: Select sugar-free formulations (e.g., sugar-free Robitussin guaifenesin) to avoid erratic blood glucose control.
EV-034.paraphrase: Insulin-treated patients: monitor blood glucose more often during acute illness; choose sugar-free formulations.

EV-035.quote: Clinicians must screen for these conditions and recommend non-anticholinergic alternatives (such as simple demulcents or topical saline sprays).
EV-035.paraphrase: Sedating antihistamines can precipitate angle-closure glaucoma and urinary retention; screen and use non-anticholinergic alternatives (e.g. simple demulcents).

EV-036.quote: Flurbiprofen lozenges and dextromethorphan must be avoided in the third trimester of pregnancy.
EV-036.paraphrase: Demulcents (simple linctus) safe throughout pregnancy and breastfeeding (preferred); dextromethorphan avoided in 3rd trimester; diphenhydramine: lactation caution (infant sedation).

EV-037.quote: Co-administration with MAOIs within 14 days of discontinuation is strictly contraindicated.
EV-037.paraphrase: Dextromethorphan + MAOIs (incl. moclobemide), SSRIs or tramadol can cause life-threatening serotonin syndrome; MAOI within 14 days is contraindicated.

EV-038.quote: Patients presenting with wheezing, shortness of breath, or bronchial tightness require immediate physical evaluation rather than non-prescription bronchodilator self-medication.
EV-038.paraphrase: Avoid OTC theophylline; wheeze, breathlessness or chest tightness need immediate physical evaluation.

EV-039.quote: the MHRA mandated the complete withdrawal of pholcodine from the UK market due to anaphylaxis risks
EV-039.paraphrase: UK context: codeine cough medicines restricted to >12 y (2015); pholcodine withdrawn (2023). Not offered by the app.

EV-040.quote: Primary risk factor for COPD (90% of cases) and lung carcinoma.
EV-040.paraphrase: Children have 7–10 cough episodes/year; smoking is the main risk factor for COPD and lung cancer.

EV-041.quote: Progressive heart failure causes ankle edema and a nocturnal productive cough with thin, frothy, pink-tinged sputum.
EV-041.paraphrase: Heart failure: nocturnal productive cough with thin, frothy, pink-tinged sputum, orthopnoea, ankle oedema.

EV-042.paraphrase: Asthma affects 10–15% of children; cough-variant asthma may present with cough alone.
